new_findings.title: trust.py 要求每个被检对象 AreAccessRulesProtected=True，与 SQLite WAL 生命周期不相容：自然 provisioning 及每次进程重启后的 -wal 重建都带继承 ACE，验证永久拒绝
evidence: wal_lifecycle2.py on real NTFS: home protected owner-only with propagating ACE; sqlite3 (journal_mode=WAL) creates state.sqlite/-wal/-shm carrying KK:(I)(F) ONLY (no foreign principals, icacls recorded); validate_private_task_home -> REJECTED 'NTFS ACL inherits permissions: ...state.sqlite'
step2 manual per-child SetAccessRuleProtection -> ACCEPTED
wal_churn.py: clean close deletes -wal; reopen recreates it with inherited ACEs -> POST-RESTART VALIDATE REJECTED 'NTFS ACL inherits permissions: ...state.sqlite-wal'

meaning: even a correctly provisioned dedicated-account deployment would self-block integration mode at the first status/run/resume call after any restart, because the check cannot be satisfied for transient SQLite children unless an operator re-protects each recreated file
new_findings.impact: Fail-closed direction (safe, no bypass demonstrated), but the enforcement as written is unsatisfiable under the real Windows ledger lifecycle and the docs provide no executable provisioning procedure. Becomes a hard Stage-2 blocker the moment real execution is enabled; today masked by the executor gate.
new_findings.reproduction: python -B wal_lifecycle2.py ; python -B wal_churn.py (disposable scratch dirs, auditor-owned)
new_findings.minimal_fix: Require inheritance protection only on the home top level; for child ledger objects verify effective Allow principals are a subset of {me, S-1-5-18, S-1-5-32-544} regardless of the inherited flag, and treat WAL/SHM recreation as expected lifecycle; or ship an idempotent provisioning tool that re-protects children and document it as a mandatory deployment step.
